data.title: End-of-Life or Unpatched Software
data.summary: Systems were running software versions that are unsupported or missing published security updates, including versions affected by vulnerabilities with public exploit code.
data.description:
Unpatched software is the most predictable finding on any infrastructure assessment, and the most reliably exploited in real incidents. Where a version is merely behind, the risk is a known vulnerability with an exploit that can be downloaded. Where it is end-of-life, no fix will ever be issued and the gap only widens.

Exploitation requires no research: the vulnerability is described, the exploit is packaged, and scanning identifies hosts at a rate that makes targeting unnecessary.

The systems involved are usually those outside routine management — appliances, embedded devices, build servers, a database nobody owns, or a legacy application whose vendor requires an old runtime.
data.recommendation:
* Maintain an inventory tied to vendor support dates, and plan replacement before end of life rather than after.
* Patch to a defined schedule with an emergency path for actively exploited vulnerabilities.
* Where a system cannot be updated, isolate it: restrict network reach, remove internet access, and monitor it specifically.
* Track the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue and prioritise against it.
data.short_recommendation: Replace unsupported software and patch to a defined schedule.
